title: Procurement & SLA acceptance / onboarding timeline - Sapphire Finance
next_steps: Zoe to send redline summary of MSA/DPA and high-level SLA by 2026-08-07
Marco to share VPC connectivity diagram and sample network playbook by 2026-08-10
Customer to confirm procurement target date and internal approvers by 2026-08-09
Schedule follow-up technical run on private deployment the week of 2026-08-17
action_items: Zoe Patel: send pricing tier spreadsheet + SSO/KMS note - due 2026-08-07
Marco Ruiz: produce network diagram + minimal firewall rules for VPC peering - due 2026-08-10
Ethan Myers: compile DPA redlines and list of non-negotiables - due 2026-08-12
Priya Nair: confirm whether on-prem connector required and give ops contact - due 2026-08-09
summary: Redwood AE and SE reviewed MSA/DPA redline expectations, SLA thresholds, pricing tiers and a tentative onboarding timeline. Customer highlighted data residency and KMS/SSO requirements; requested a short network playbook and explicit egress cost estimate. Agreed to follow-up with redline summary and a technical run to validate VPC/private deployment feasibility.
transcript: [00:00] Zoe Patel (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Lina, Ethan, Priya and Carlos on — awesome. We'll do a quick agenda, go over MSA/DPA open items, SLA thresholds, and then Marco will walk through the VPC/private deployment preflight.
[00:12] Lina Cho (Sapphire): Thanks Zoe. We got a tight clock here — procurement wants a go/no-go estimate this month. So today is mainly to understand blockers on security and pricing.
[00:27] Zoe: Totally. Quick intro from Marco — SE who'll handle the network and infra details.

[00:35] Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE): Morning, hi. I'll cover VPC peering, KMS options, and sample latency numbers. Also we have a draft SLA — I want to walk through the SLOs to make sure they map to your acceptance criteria.

[00:48] Ethan Myers (Legal): Hi all. From legal side, DPA redlines are the sticking point; we have a couple of data retention asks and some processor-subprocessor visibility requirements. We'll list them but want to know your MSA risk posture first.

[01:02] Zoe: Understood. High level — Redwood offers hosted and private options. For regulated workloads like yours we typically go Dedicated or Private (VPC or on-prem). We can accept standard DPA terms with a few commercial exceptions — we can capture those as redlines. We'll send a summary after the call.
[01:21] Carlos Vega (FinOps): Can you talk about egress fees? We run heavy inference and need to model monthly spend with realistic token and embedding rates.

[01:33] Zoe: Sure, we'll include a tiered pricing spreadsheet. Quick note: egress charging depends on whether you're on our hosted cluster vs. private in your VPC — I'll flag the expected ranges. We'll give both conservative and optimized numbers.
[01:48] Priya Nair (Infra): On KMS — we require customer-managed keys, ideally HSM-backed. Also SSO/SAML integration is mandatory for us. Any blockers there?

[01:59] Marco: We support customer-managed KMS (via KMS/HSM integrations) and SAML SSO. For Private deployments we can either integrate with your KMS or provide a key-wrapping flow. For hosted accounts, we offer envelope encryption with customer key control options. There's a bit of work on the onboarding side but no hard blocker.
[02:20] Ethan: About the DPA — subprocessor list, and SOC2 evidence. We need an audit trail: can you provide artifact references?

[02:31] Zoe: Yes we can share SOC 2 Type II report, security whitepaper and our subprocessors list. I'll attach links in the follow-up. Note that some product names in the docs may be slightly outdated — apologies, the CI pipeline had a rename so the doc may reference Redwood Serving v2 instead of our internal name.
[02:56] Lina: That happens. Main thing is timeline — procurement wants a final contract signed by Aug 20. Is that achievable?
[03:05] Zoe: If we can get redlines and a clear list of non-negotiables within a week, Aug 20 is feasible. We'll need signatures path and how many legal approvers you have.
[03:18] Lina: Two approvers: procurement and counsel. Carlos will sign off on pricing. We'll aim to turn quickly if we have the SSO/KMS answers.

[03:29] Marco: On the SLA, two points: uptime SLA (we typically offer 99.9% for Dedicated, 99.95 for Enterprise private). Latency SLOs depend on model and instance sizing; for small LLMs we can deliver p95 sub-200ms gen token latency in Dedicated, but for large open models higher — we should map to your critical routes.
[03:55] Carlos: We care about both p95 latency for customer-facing inference and cost per 1M tokens. Can you give an example calc for a 3M token month?
[04:07] Zoe: We'll send example line items. Quick placeholder — with a mixed model fleet and batching you might see $X–$Y per 1M tokens. Marco, we'll attach an optimized case and a conservative case.
[04:22] Marco: Yup. Also TTLs for KV cache, if you need session-level cache retention for chat, that affects memory and cost.
[04:31] Priya: For network connectivity: we need minimal firewall rules and egress ranges to open to your managed endpoints. Can you provide a network playbook?

[04:41] Marco: Absolutely — I'll prepare a one-pager with CIDR ranges, ports, and sample VPC peering commands. We'll include a short checklist for routing, NAT, and peering. That's one of the deliverables we talked about.
[04:56] Ethan: Back to the DPA — data retention and delete-on-demand for PII. Can you confirm deletion guarantees and audit logs?

[05:06] Zoe: We maintain deletion API and event audit logs. For Private deployments you can control retention more tightly. For Hosted we'll provide documented delete flows and confirm event logs are available for the retention window in the DPA.
[05:20] Lina: Excellent. I heard mention of on-prem connector — what does that look like?

[05:27] Marco: On-prem connector is a small agent that establishes secure outbound tunnels to our control plane; it's used in air-gapped or highly regulated environments. For Sapphire, if you want everything inside your VPC, we can run the model serving nodes in your cloud account with our control plane managing deployments. There's an ops integration step.
[05:48] Carlos: That sounds like Dedicated in our account?
[05:51] Marco: Yes, Dedicated or Private VPC. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our infra but isolated to you; Private runs in your cloud account.
[06:00] Zoe: Quick check — any immediate showstoppers?
[06:03] Priya: No showstoppers. Need the KMS implementation detail and the minimal open ports to sign the network change window.
[06:11] Zoe: We'll deliver.
[06:15] [07:00] (pause / side chatter as documents are pulled)
[07:05] Ethan: One legal nuance — indemnity caps. We will push for higher cap for regulated workloads. Are you open to a negotiation here?

[07:16] Zoe: Generally we have standard caps in the MSA. If it's material we can escalate to commercial legal — we usually see a counter-proposal rather than a flat rejection. We'll note that and include guidance to your team when we send the redline summary.
[07:29] Lina: Okay. Also we need the SLA to include failover behavior — what's your fallback if a region has degraded performance?

[07:38] Marco: Smart routing will failover to a compatible model variant in another region, but it depends on latency tolerance. We'll document the fallback policy and expected cold-start time. For critical routes we recommend regional standby capacity or Dedicated throughput to avoid cross-region fallbacks.
[07:58] Carlos: And how do rollouts work? Canary? A/B? I want to avoid regression costs.
[08:07] Zoe: We support canary and staged rollouts with automatic rollback on quality regressions. Redwood Optimize can monitor quality signals and trigger alerts if eval sets degrade.
[08:19] Priya: Eval sets — will you let us upload our prompt set for regression checks?
[08:24] Marco: Yes, you can provide prompt sets and we can run pre/post comparisons. We'll include that in the onboarding checklist.
[08:33] Ethan: A question about subprocessors — can you provide an explicit list and commit to notification windows if you add a new one?

[08:41] Zoe: Standard practice is to share the current list and notify impacted customers. We'll include the subprocessors list in the follow-up pack. If any subprocessor is controversial you can request a replacement or mitigation.
[08:57] Lina: Procurement timeline recap — if we get redlines by Aug 7 and the tech run is week of Aug 17, we can route for signature by Aug 20. Any risks?

[09:07] Zoe: The risks are DPA negotiations and any unusual KMS/SSO custom work. If Ethan's redlines are within typical limits we can move forward quickly. If there are non-standard indemnity or escrow asks it'll take longer.
[09:21] Ethan: We'll try to keep it scoped. I'll compile a short list of must-haves vs nice-to-haves and share by end of week.
[09:28] Marco: For the technical run, we'll need a small dataset and a sample request shape. We can do a dry run across a small model to validate latency and KV cache behavior.
[09:40] Priya: Can you run a 1k concurrent short chat session sim to show throughput?
[09:45] Marco: We can simulate load, yes — we'll coordinate with your ops window.
[09:51] Zoe: I'll also send a pricing snapshot with committed capacity vs on-demand estimates, and highlight where Dedicated reduces unit cost.
[09:59] Carlos: On billing — do you support monthly invoices with net-30?
[10:03] Zoe: Yes, standard is Net-30 for enterprise, we can discuss escrow or changes in procurement paperwork if needed.
[10:10] (crosstalk) Priya: There's a subtle point about egress when models are hosted outside our cloud, how do you surface that cost?

[10:16] Zoe: We'll include an egress model line in the spreadsheet. For Private in your account egress is internal so minimal; for Hosted there is egress per GB from model endpoints — we will provide both numbers.
[10:30] Marco: Also note that tokenization overhead varies between models; we can recommend smaller models or quantized variants if you want to reduce cost.
[10:40] Lina: Are there any references / customers in regulated finance you can share?
[10:45] Zoe: We can share Redacted case studies and references under NDA. I'll include contact handles in the follow-up pack.
[10:53] Ethan: On the SLA specifics — what is the credits model for downtime? and is it capped?

[10:59] Zoe: Our SLA crediting is pro-rata and typically capped (we'll include exact language). For Dedicated higher uptime tiers reduce credit frequency. We'll propose language for your counsel to review.
[11:10] Marco: If you're on Private with local control, we can map maintenance windows to your ops cadence to avoid surprises.
[11:18] Lina: That helps. Anything else on technical gating?
[11:22] Marco: We'll flag one more item — KV cache warming and session affinity. If you rely on long-lived sessions we recommend sticky routing to maintain low tail latency.
[11:33] Carlos: Ok we'll review. Zoe, can you include a short runbook for on-call escalation paths?
[11:39] Zoe: Yes, contact matrix and escalation steps will be in the onboarding pack.
[11:46] [20:00] (brief pause while participants review an SLA draft link) Link: https://redwood.support/sla-draft (note: internal placeholder)
[20:12] Ethan: I see SLA draft. One edit — clarify maintenance window attribution so that planned maintenance doesn't trigger credits. Also want a formal RTO for failed nodes.
[20:22] Zoe: We can add planned maintenance carve-outs and propose an RTO; will include proposed numbers.
[20:30] Lina: Action items from our side: we'll circulate the procurement approver list and internal timeline by Friday.
[20:37] Zoe: Great. We'll do the redline summary and send the network playbook. Marco will also propose a test plan for the week of Aug 17.
[20:46] Marco: Test plan includes: small load test (1k concurrent simulated sessions), VPC peering validation, KMS integration smoke test, and a latency/throughput readout.
[20:59] Priya: Do you need any privileged accounts from us to test SSO?
[21:04] Marco: We'll need a test SAML IdP entry and a persona with standard permissions, plus a temporary KMS test key or a staging key exchange flow.
[21:14] Ethan: I will still compile DPA redlines and distinguish must-haves; expect that by EOD Friday.
[21:21] Zoe: Perfect. Anything else?
[21:25] Lina: No, that's it from procurement for now. Appreciate the clear next steps.

[21:30] Zoe: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack: MSA/DPA redline summary, SLA draft with credit language, pricing spreadsheet, network playbook, and proposed test plan. Meeting notes and action items will be in CRM.
[21:48] (meeting close)
